key_insight: A physics-guided neural differential equation reduced-order model can capture nonlinear, multi-mode aeroelastic coupling and oscillatory buffet dynamics with far less cost than full CFD.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster prediction of aeroelastic stability, lock-in, and limit-cycle oscillations for transonic flows, which is valuable for aircraft design and flutter/buffet assessment.
method: Combines a nonlinear fluid oscillator with a finite-memory multi-input Volterra series.
Adds a compact neural network correction to improve accuracy for oscillatory flow dynamics.
Generalizes aerodynamic coupling to multiple structural modes and is trained from one prescribed-motion CFD case.
evidence_signal: The ROM was evaluated on transonic buffet over the ONERA OAT15A airfoil and showed good agreement with reference solutions for aeroelastic stability, frequency lock-in, and limit-cycle amplitudes.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of the training excitation and may degrade when extrapolating beyond the learned motion envelope or mode combinations.
paper_title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for Oscillatory Flows in Aeroelasticity with Application to Transonic Buffet
